components.name: DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 rack
components.description: A rack-scale system whose GPUs are connected by NVLink through the NVLink passive copper cable cartridge backplane. It holds compute trays, NVLink switch trays, top-of-rack management switches, power shelves, a bus bar and liquid cooling manifolds.
components.function: Forms a single 72-GPU NVLink domain. NVLink is the scale-up fabric inside the rack, InfiniBand the scale-out fabric between racks, and Ethernet carries storage, management and external traffic.

steps.text: Before you start: the power shelves are energized, the top-of-rack switches are active and NMX-M services are available. Check them in Base Command Manager.
Power on the NVLink switch trays first, from Base Command Manager. Each one boots with rack-specific configuration, so the NVLink fabric is up before any GPU needs it.
Then power on the compute trays. While they boot, Base Command Manager checks that the latest OS updates and configuration are installed.
A booting compute tray checks for OS updates over the network: it installs them before booting, or boots quickly from local storage if there are none.
The compute trays then connect to the switch trays, storage and the other compute trays. Power operations are orchestrated through NVIDIA Mission Control.

Use it after the first software install, after firmware upgrades, before full rack diagnostics, and after replacing a compute tray, switch tray, trunk link or cable cartridge. NVIDIA recommends doing it through Mission Control. You need the IP addresses of all BMCs, hosts and power shelves.
Turn off AC power to all power shelves (they can go off in parallel), then wait three to five minutes for the PSU capacitors to discharge. Skip this on the very first power-up.
Ping all compute and switch tray BMCs and OS addresses to make sure none of them answers.
Turn on AC power to all power shelves, in parallel. Wait two minutes for the compute and switch tray BMCs to power up, then ping all BMC addresses until they answer.
Let the switch trays boot to NVOS and wait two more minutes.

Provision the switch trays. For L11 diagnostics, log in to each switch tray and check its health. For a multi-node workload, repeat the cluster provisioning, then set up and start the NMX-C services and run the health checks.
Power on all compute nodes from the compute tray BMCs. Wait five minutes, ping the compute nodes, then run the post-reboot verification.
Power off all compute trays through their BMCs (IPMI, Redfish or another supported API).

software.name: NVIDIA Mission Control
software.description: Workload-aware orchestration with full-stack observability: job and power-profile management, topology-aware scheduling, fast checkpointing and autonomous job recovery, health checks, and leak detection through building-management integration. Power operations and firmware updates are orchestrated through it.
software.note: Cluster-level software; the guide does not say which node it runs on.

software.name: Base Command Manager (BCM)
software.description: Manages all system components: powers trays on and off, manages the operating system images that compute trays boot, and reaches the out-of-band interfaces over ipminet.
software.note: Section 2.2: ipminet gives Base Command Manager and the head node access to the out-of-band/BMC interfaces in the rack. Where the head node sits is not stated.

software.name: CUDA
software.description: The CUDA platform: more than 150 libraries and the tools to optimize and debug GPU-accelerated applications, which use the NVLink network to distribute work across every GPU in the rack.

software.name: Internode Memory Exchange (IMEX)
software.description: Maps GPU memory over NVLink between GPUs across OS boundaries in an NVLink domain, using memory export and import. Started on all nodes in the domain at system startup or at CUDA job launch; communicates across nodes over the compute node network.
software.note: The guide says it runs exclusively on compute nodes.

software.name: NVIDIA Switch OS (NVOS)
software.description: The operating system of the NVLink switch tray, with a CLI and OpenAPI (Swagger) management. It includes the NVLink Subnet Manager, Fabric Manager, NMX-Controller, NMX-Telemetry and the NVSwitch firmware.

software.name: NMX-Controller
software.description: Cluster application for fabric software-defined networking; in DGX VR racks its services are the subnet manager and Fabric Manager.

software.name: Fabric Manager
software.description: Configures routing among NVSwitch ports and the GPU-side routing, coordinates with the GPU driver to initialize the GPUs, and monitors the fabric for NVLink and NVSwitch errors.

software.name: NVLink Subnet Manager (NVLSM)
software.description: Discovers the NVLink topology, assigns LIDs to GPU and NVSwitch NVLink ports, programs the switch forwarding tables and the partition keys, and monitors changes in the NVLink fabric.

software.name: NMX-Telemetry
software.description: Collects and aggregates telemetry from all the NVLink switches in an NVLink domain.

software.name: DOCA
software.description: Framework for applications and services that offload, accelerate and isolate data center workloads on BlueField. DOCA-Host includes the host drivers and tools for the BlueField and ConnectX devices in the rack.

software.name: NCCL, NVSHMEM and UCX
software.description: Inter-GPU communication libraries over PCIe, NVLink, NVLink Multi-node, InfiniBand and RoCE: NCCL's topology-aware collectives, NVSHMEM's partitioned global address space, and UCX's messaging and remote memory access.

software.name: Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM)
software.description: Manages and monitors data center GPUs and NVSwitches: active health monitoring, diagnostics, alerts, and power and clock policies.

software.name: NVIDIA Firmware Tools (MFT)
software.description: Network ASIC firmware management: build a standard or custom firmware image, query firmware information, and flash an image. Shipped with the DGX VR software release.
software.note: The guide says 'network ASIC'; which devices that covers is read as the ConnectX-9 and BlueField-4.

software.name: NVIDIA System Management (NVSM)
software.description: Diagnostics and management: determines system health, identifies component issues and alerts, and runs stress tests. 'sudo nvsm show health' gives the overall health summary.

software.name: NVDEBUG
software.description: Collects BMC event logs, firmware versions, hardware inventory and system health data into one archive for NVIDIA support.

commands.title: Virtual A/C Cycle
commands.purpose: Simulates a power drop (like pulling and reinserting the power cord) without physically disconnecting the power.

commands.title: Graceful Shutdown
commands.purpose: Initiates a clean shutdown of the host system, allowing the operating system to properly terminate all services and processes.

commands.title: Force Power Off
commands.purpose: Immediately cuts power to the host without waiting for the OS to shut down.

commands.title: Power On Host
commands.purpose: Turns the host on.

commands.title: Power Cycle Host
commands.purpose: Performs a full power cycle (off and then back on).

commands.title: Set Power Restore Policy: Always Off
commands.purpose: After power loss, the system will remain off when power is restored.

source.section: 6.4.1.1.6 Set Power Restore Policy: Always Off

commands.title: Set Power Restore Policy: Last State
commands.purpose: After power loss, the system will return to its previous state (on or off) when power is restored.

source.section: 6.4.1.1.7 Set Power Restore Policy: Last State

commands.title: Set Power Restore Policy: Always On
commands.purpose: After power loss, the system will automatically power on when power is restored.

source.section: 6.4.1.1.8 Set Power Restore Policy: Always On

commands.title: HMC Graceful Restart
commands.purpose: Performs a controlled restart of the HMC, allowing it to shut down services cleanly before rebooting. This is the preferred method for most maintenance scenarios.

commands.title: HMC Force Restart
commands.purpose: Immediately restarts the HMC without waiting for services to shut down gracefully.
commands.note: Warning: This is not recommended except in emergency situations, as it may lead to a host restart or data loss.

commands.title: BMC Reset
commands.purpose: Performs a forced reset of the BMC. This operation is typically used after firmware updates or if the BMC becomes unresponsive.

commands.title: Firmware Bundle Update
commands.purpose: Uploads and applies a firmware bundle to the system. Set FILENAME to the path of the firmware bundle. The following command uses a multipart form upload to send the update file to the BMC.

commands.title: Get Firmware Versions (with expand)
commands.purpose: Retrieves detailed firmware version information for all components, using the $expand query with $levels=1 to include nested inventory data. The dollar signs are escaped (\$) so the shell does not treat them as variables.

commands.title: Check BMC Firmware Signing Type
commands.purpose: Checks the signing type of the BMC firmware image, which helps confirm the authenticity and security of the installed firmware.
commands.command:
curl -k -u "root:openBmc" -X GET \
     "https://${bmcip}/redfish/v1/Chassis/ERoT_BMC_0/Oem/NvidiaRoT/RoTProtectedComponents/BMC_0/ImageSlots/<active image slot>" \
     | grep SigningType
commands.note: Replace <active image slot> with the active slot ID. To find it, read the ActiveSlotId property from /redfish/v1/Chassis/ERoT_BMC_0/Oem/NvidiaRoT/RoTProtectedComponents/BMC_0.

commands.title: Check HMC Firmware Signing Type
commands.purpose: Checks the signing type of the HMC firmware image.
commands.command:
curl -k -u "root:openBmc" -X GET \
     "https://${bmcip}/redfish/v1/Chassis/HGX_ERoT_BMC_0/Oem/NvidiaRoT/RoTProtectedComponents/HGX_BMC_0/ImageSlots/<active image slot>" \
     | grep SigningType
commands.note: Replace <active image slot> with the active slot ID. To find it, read the ActiveSlotId property from /redfish/v1/Chassis/HGX_ERoT_BMC_0/Oem/NvidiaRoT/RoTProtectedComponents/HGX_BMC_0.

commands.title: Enabling Global Write Protect
commands.purpose: Enables hardware write protection for the system.

commands.title: Disabling Global Write Protect
commands.purpose: Disables hardware write protection for the system.

commands.title: Reading Global Write Protect
commands.purpose: Reads the current hardware write protection status.
commands.note: Enabling write protection is recommended after firmware updates or configuration changes to prevent accidental or unauthorized modifications.

commands.title: Creating a New Account
commands.purpose: Creates a new user account with the specified username, password, and role.
commands.note: You can set RoleId to Administrator, Operator, or ReadOnly based on the required access level for the user.

commands.title: Updating Password for an Existing Account
commands.purpose: Updates the password for an existing account, such as the root user.

source.section: 6.4.1.5.2 Updating Password for an Existing Account

commands.note: Replace CURRENT_PASSWORD with the current password for the account, and NEW_PASSWORD with the desired new password.

commands.title: Clear HMC Event Log
commands.purpose: Clears all entries from the HMC event log. Use this command after reviewing or archiving log data to maintain log clarity and free up space.

commands.title: Clear BMC Event Log
commands.purpose: Removes all entries from the BMC event log. This is useful for resetting the log after resolving issues or before starting new troubleshooting steps.

commands.title: Reset BMC to Factory Defaults
commands.purpose: Restores the BMC to its original factory settings. All user configurations and custom settings will be lost. Use this if the BMC is unresponsive or you need to clear all settings.

commands.title: Reset HMC to Factory Defaults
commands.purpose: Resets the Host Management Controller (HMC) to its factory default configuration. This will remove all custom settings and user data from the HMC.

commands.title: Clear the eMMC (This Will Clear the Journal)
commands.purpose: Securely erases the eMMC storage, including the system journal. Use this operation with caution, as it will permanently delete all data stored on the eMMC.

source.section: 6.4.1.7.3 Clear the eMMC (This Will Clear the Journal)

commands.title: Reset SBIOS to Defaults
commands.purpose: Restores the system BIOS (SBIOS) settings to their factory defaults. This can help resolve configuration issues or prepare the system for a fresh deployment.

commands.title: IPMI - Host SOL Access
commands.purpose: Establishes a Serial Over LAN (SOL) session to the host using IPMI. This allows you to interact with the system console remotely, even if the OS is not running.
commands.command: ipmitool -C 17 -H ${bmcip} -U root -P OpenBmc -I lanplus sol activate

commands.title: SSH - Host SOL Access
commands.purpose: Provides SSH access to the host’s SOL interface. This is an alternative to IPMI SOL for remote console access.

commands.title: Disable IPMI
commands.purpose: Disables the IPMI protocol on the BMC. This is recommended for enhanced security if IPMI remote management is not required.

commands.title: Capturing Debug Logs with NVDEBUG
commands.purpose: When troubleshooting complex issues or working with NVIDIA support, it is often necessary to collect detailed debug logs from the compute tray. The preferred method for capturing and packaging these logs is to use the NVDEBUG tool, which gathers all relevant system, firmware, and event logs into a single archive for analysis.
commands.note: Steps in 6.4.1.11.1: 1. Access the BMC or host system where NVDEBUG is available. Ensure you have the necessary permissions to run diagnostic tools. 2. Run the NVDEBUG tool according to your system's documentation; replace /path/to/save/debug-logs.tar.gz with your desired output location. 3. Transfer the log archive to your support contact or upload it as instructed by NVIDIA support. NVDEBUG automatically collects a comprehensive set of logs, including BMC event logs, firmware versions, hardware inventory, and system health data. This is the recommended approach for efficient and complete log collection.

commandNotes.usage: Set the BMC address first (export bmcip="192.168.1.100") or replace ${bmcip} by hand. The examples use example credentials; replace them with your BMC credentials.
commandNotes.factoryReset: After a BMC factory reset the default username and password are admin/admin, and you are asked to change them at the first login. Change default credentials immediately.

safety.title: Batteries
safety.text: Danger of explosion if the battery is replaced incorrectly: use only the battery the manufacturer recommends. Do not recharge, disassemble or puncture it, and dispose of it according to local rules.

safety.title: Electrostatic discharge
safety.text: ESD can damage drives, boards and other parts. Work at an ESD workstation or wear an antistatic wrist strap, and hold boards only by their edges.

safety.title: Power supplies
safety.text: A power supply has no user-serviceable parts and hazardous voltage, current and energy inside: do not open it. When replacing a hot-plug power supply, unplug the power cord of that supply before removing it.

safety.title: Standby power
safety.text: The power button does not completely turn off AC power: standby power is active whenever the system is plugged in.

safety.title: Working in the rack
safety.text: The rack must be anchored so it cannot tip when equipment is extended. Extend only one piece of equipment from the rack at a time.

safety.title: Moving and lifting
safety.text: Follow local occupational health and safety rules, and use mechanical or other suitable assistance when moving and lifting equipment.

safety.title: Hot parts
safety.text: If the system has been running, processors and heat sinks may be hot. Let the system cool before opening the covers.

safety.title: Covers and airflow
safety.text: Operate the system only with its covers installed, after checking that no loose tools or parts are left inside.

glossary.definition: An NVIDIA rack with a 72-GPU NVL domain.

A high-speed, low-latency interconnect technology designed to overcome PCIe bandwidth limitations in multi-GPU and GPU-to-CPU communication. It enables unified memory access across GPUs and scales through NVSwitch chips.
Chips that act as non-blocking switches between servers, through which NVLink scales to create high-bandwidth fabrics.
In-network computing in NVSwitch that accelerates collective operations by performing computations within the network.
The high-bandwidth, low-latency scale-out compute fabric between racks.
Handles storage, management (in-band and out-of-band) and external connectivity.
Together with the HMC, provides out-of-band management of the compute tray hardware resources. External access is available through standard BMC and console interfaces.
Together with the BMC, provides out-of-band management of the compute tray hardware resources.
Out-of-band management of the compute tray hardware resources is provided by the BMC and HMC microcontrollers.
Top-of-rack switches connect all BMCs in the compute trays (including BlueField-4 BMCs) and the switch trays to the management network.

A component you can replace yourself: the E1.S NVMe cache drive, the compute tray battery, the NVLink Switch tray battery, the power supply unit (PSU) and the power shelf management module. An authorized NVIDIA representative must replace components that are not on this list.
A customer-replaceable unit in the power shelf.
ESD can damage drives, boards and other parts. NVIDIA recommends doing all procedures at an ESD workstation, or else wearing an antistatic wrist strap attached to chassis ground.

The operating system on the NVLink switch tray. It enables the management and configuration of NVIDIA switch system platforms through a command-line interface (CLI) and OpenAPI (Swagger), and includes NVLSM, Fabric Manager and the NVSwitch firmware.

Discovers the NVLink network topology, assigns logical identifiers to GPU and NVSwitch NVLink ports, calculates and programs the switch forwarding table, programs the partition key for NVLink partitions and monitors changes in the NVLink fabric.
Configures the NVSwitch memory fabrics to form a large memory fabric among the participating GPUs and monitors the NVLinks that support the fabric.
A secure service that maps GPU memory over NVLink between the GPUs in an NVLink domain across the OS/node boundary, using memory export and import operations.
Provides topology-aware inter-GPU communication primitives: collective communication and point-to-point send/receive for intra- and inter-node data transfers.
A suite of tools that manage and monitor NVIDIA data center GPUs and NVSwitches in cluster environments.
A set of network ASIC firmware management tools that generate, query and flash firmware images.
Manages all system components; it is used to power on the NVLink switch trays first, then the compute trays.
A session that lets you use the host system console remotely, even if the OS is not running.
The system BIOS of the compute tray. Its settings can be restored to their factory defaults.
